metadata.title: Assessing digital self-efficacy: Review and scale development

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a German web-based quota sample administered in August 2020 (CASI) with a 3-form planned missing design, where all participants received a common block (X) and only subsets received validation items (A/B/C). The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures; therefore, population-representativeness beyond the quota design cannot be assumed. Missingness in the validation measures is handled via the planned-missing design and estimation in Mplus using full information maximum likelihood (FIML), rather than by applying survey weights. Analytically, the authors also excluded invalid response patterns (ipsativized variance, Mahalanobis distance, and implausibly short response times) before fitting confirmatory factor models and conducting measurement invariance tests.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) are not applicable because the study does not analyze ILSA cognitive achievement outcomes with PV-based scoring; instead, it develops and validates a self-efficacy scale using Likert-type items and latent variable modeling. Missing data handling is not reported in the schema sense because the paper describes FIML for missingness by design (planned missing), which is not one of the allowed missing-data handling categories in the extraction schema. The study’s missingness approach is therefore outside the schema’s discrete mapping, even though the authors provide sufficient methodological detail for FIML estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Validation study sample was drawn in Germany via a web-based CASI quota sample (initial N=627). Respondents were included only if they completed the full questionnaire (no premature abort). The authors excluded invalid cases using three simultaneous criteria: (a) ipsativized variance below the bottom 5% of the sampling distribution, (b) Mahalanobis distance above the top 2.5% of the sampling distribution, and (c) implausibly short average response times (<1 second per item). The final analytic sample for the main analyses consisted of N=571. For test-retest reliability, the same items were administered to a subsample (n=147) about 6 weeks later, and after applying the same invalid-case screening, the final pretest sample was n=137.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICILS 2013 the study leveraged Gender, Age, Education level to predict problem-solving, finding that This paper is primarily a scale-development and validation study rather than an ILSA predictive-ML study. The authors conducted (1) a scoping review of existing digital self-efficacy (DSE) measures (n=17 included studies) and (2) the development and validation of a new German-language multidimensional DSE scale aligned to DigComp 2.1. The validation study used a German web-based CASI quota sample with a planned-missing design (initial N=627; final analytic N=571) and excluded invalid response patterns based on ipsativized variance, Mahalanobis distance, and implausibly short response times. Using Mplus with robust maximum likelihood and FIML for planned-missing data, confirmatory factor analysis supported a first-order correlated-factor structure over a single g-factor model, with standardized factor loadings mostly >0.50. Reliability (McDonald’s Omega) was high for information/data literacy (Ω=0.887), communication/collaboration (Ω=0.749), digital content creation (Ω=0.811), and safety (Ω=0.921), and moderate for problem-solving (Ω=0.659). Measurement invariance across gender was supported via (partial) strict invariance, enabling gender comparisons using manifest scale scores. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse for ML-specific fields because the manuscript does not train or compare machine-learning predictive models. Instead, it performs scoping review synthesis and psychometric scale development/validation using confirmatory factor analysis and measurement invariance testing. Consequently, PV handling and missing-data handling are not mapped to the ILSA PV schema, and ml_techniques are intentionally left empty.
